title: Nora and the Best Path
markdown:
Nora loved numbers. Her room was filled with geometric shapes and colourful graphs. Today the challenge was more pressing. Aunt Willow, who lived beyond the Whispering Woods, was unwell. The medicine was ready. Time was short.

The usual courier, a hedgehog named Fern, had a problem. Heavy rain had turned the forest paths into slippery mud. The main road was a swirling river. On top of that, Fern was swamped. Because the rain kept villagers indoors, requests piled higher than a squirrel’s winter hoard. He’d dash for one delivery, then remember another on the opposite side of the woods, backtracking through mud. A bottleneck. Everything slowed to a crawl.

Nora watched him, nose twitching with frustration, scurrying back and forth, sighs lost in the drumming rain. It looked like a chaotic jumble of numbers changing places.

She sat a moment on the porch step. Rain stitched the garden. A single leaf turned in the gutter and did not hurry. Fern’s tiny tracks crossed themselves in the mud, a map of wasted effort. Coach Dev ambled by, comforting as a warm coat. He saw Nora’s thoughtful frown and Fern’s frantic scurrying.

“Fern is trying to deliver each package one by one. Look, Nora. Many of his deliveries are close together. Some houses are practically on the way to others.”

Nora’s eyes widened. Not a jumble of individual trips. Connected locations. A network waiting to be untangled.

Coach Dev smiled. “Sometimes, instead of doing each little step separately, you can group them. Find the most efficient way to get from one point to the next, without going back and forth. If you have to visit three friends in a row, would you go all the way home between each visit?”

“Optimisation,” Nora said. The word buzzed. She’d learned it in maths club — making a process work with less wasted motion. Finding an elegant route, not a louder one.

With Nora’s charts and Coach Dev’s questions, they helped Fern. Nora sketched a new route on a broad leaf. “Instead of going here for one delivery and then backtracking for another, we group them. Edge of the woods first — Aunt Willow’s medicine. Then a slight turn to Mr Fitzwilliam’s cottage, next door, on the same circuit. Connected stops. No wasted movement.”

Fern looked at the sketch and his satchel, whiskers twitching with hope. “So instead of running everywhere… I run somewhere, and visit many friends along the way?”

“Exactly,” Coach Dev said. “You’re optimising the route. Individual trips become one planned journey. The whole picture, not just the pieces.”

The plan worked. Fern followed Nora’s sequence with determined steps. The rain thinned to mist. He delivered Aunt Willow’s medicine, then Mr Fitzwilliam’s tonic, then the baker’s yeast, all with a new rhythm. The satchel felt lighter because the path was lighter.

When Fern returned, tired, eyes sparkling. “Nora — I delivered three times as much, and I even found a shortcut to the berry patch.”

Nora beamed. “When you understand the principle, you can make the world work a little better. A messy problem. A cleaner path.”

Coach Dev nodded. Fern started asking Nora to help plan all his deliveries. Nora was delighted. Who wouldn’t want an elegant solution, especially when it meant helping a friend? She wondered what other clever paths were waiting, hidden in plain sight, in the rain-dark wood and the numbers on her wall.
characters: Nora (a maths competitor), Fern (a hedgehog), Dev (a coach)
author: StoryGen Community
